title: Pars I close: Le Blanc kept common Reformed doctrine; Rome's four imputations are calumny; opponent's charges fall
source_text: CXLV. Jam ergo clarum est, & abunde probatum, me in Thesibus, quas arguit vir Doctus, communem Scholae Reformatae doctrinam non deseruisse, nec privatam quandam sententiam, pro doctrina in eorum Scholis recepta falso obtrusisse: nec injuria de Scholae Romanae Doctoribus me questum esse, quod per calumniam Reformatis imputent quatuor illa, de quibus hactenus prolixe actum est, quasi communi consensu ab illis doceantur: adeoque Virum Doctum immerito me dolosae dissimulationis, & animi parum synceri accusasse; & mihi ipsi crimen calumniae impegisse, quod injuste & absque ratione Scholae Romanae Doctores, ut Reformatos hac in parte calumniantes traducam. Unde sequitur varias conclusiones & declamationes, quas tam putri fundamento inaedificat vir facundissimus per se corruere & evanescere, ut non opus sit singula minutatim excutere & persequi.
pass_a_gloss: Now therefore it is clear, and abundantly proved, that in the Theses which the Learned Man argues against I have not deserted the common doctrine of the Reformed School, nor falsely thrust forward some private opinion as the doctrine received in their Schools: nor have I complained unjustly of the Doctors of the Roman School, that through calumny they impute to the Reformed those four things concerning which action has thus far been taken at length, as if they were taught by them by common consent: and therefore that the Learned Man has undeservedly accused me of deceitful dissimulation and of a mind too little sincere; and has fastened on me myself the crime of calumny, because I unjustly and without reason traduce the Doctors of the Roman School as calumniating the Reformed on this point. Whence it follows that the various conclusions and declamations which the most eloquent man builds upon so rotten a foundation collapse and vanish of themselves, so that there is no need to examine and pursue each minutely.
pass_b_english: Pars I close: Le Blanc has not deserted common Reformed doctrine or foisted a private opinion as school teaching.
His complaint stands: Rome calumniously imputes the four points as if by Reformed common consent.
The opponent's charges of deceitful dissimulation and of Le Blanc's own calumny are undeserved; the eloquent declamations built on that rotten base collapse without needing a line-by-line chase.
